claim.why_it_matters: 12.3.8.4 General rule 11 is a three-alternative cascade (a / b / c) exactly parallel to General rule 10 for program prototypes, which the markdown does render as three items. Here the third alternative is swallowed into the text of the second, so GR 11 appears to have only two sub-rules and 'otherwise, c) the details are taken from the external repository' reads as continuation prose of rule b) rather than as the independent fallback rule that governs function resolution from the external repository. The page-339 markdown slice consequently opens at item 12), leaving no item c) anywhere in the list.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered both pages at 300 dpi and compared against specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 14621-14655 directly. NO TEXT IS LOST AND NO ENUMERATOR GLYPH IS LOST. (1) Glyph check, as required for a claimed lost choice indicator: PDF page 339 (printed folio 309) opens with a hanging-indent sub-item whose printed glyphs are exactly 'c)' at the same left column as the 'a)' and 'b)' markers on page 338, followed by 'the details are taken from the external repository for the function with the same name as the externalized name of the function prototype. That function is the one that will be activated.' The markdown at line 14648 retains those same glyphs 'c)' verbatim, immediately after 'otherwise, ', and then the sentence word-for-word identical to the PDF, including the terminal 'That function is the one that will be activated.' Character-for-character the c) rule and its label survive intact. (2) The claim's load-bearing justification is therefore FALSE: 'leaving no item c) anywhere in the list' is contradicted by the markdown, which contains 'c)' plus its full text. A reader (or a citation of 12.3.8.4 GR 11 c)) finds the rule exactly where the cascade puts it, third and last, introduced by its own surviving 'c)' marker, and reads the same normative meaning as the PDF: the external-repository fallback for function resolution. (3) What actually differs is a single missing paragraph break/indent at the b)->c) boundary, plus the sentence sitting in the page-338 slice instead of the page-339 slice. Both are artifacts of reflowing a paragraph across a page break, which is exactly the page-break furniture / line-wrapping class of difference this check is instructed to reject. The transcription demonstrably reflows across page boundaries as a matter of convention: the continuation paragraph that physically opens PDF page 338 ('name-2 is the interface specified for interface-name-3 ... interface-specifier.') is not in the page-338 slice at all but folded back into GR 8 on the page-337 side at line 14621, complete with the tell-tale dehyphenation artifact 'interface- name-2'. Content migrating backward across this particular page seam is the transcription behaving as designed, not misplacement. (4) No semantic content, no rule, no qualifier and no cross-reference differs between the two sources at this location. Rejected.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a content discrepancy. The whole of 12.3.8.4 GR 11 item c) is present in the markdown, verbatim, with its 'c)' choice indicator intact; the PDF's page-339 opening glyphs are 'c)' and the markdown preserves them. The only difference is cosmetic: the newline and 4-space indent that would set c) off as its own list item were dropped when the paragraph was reflowed across the 338/339 page break, so c) trails b) on one line inside the page-338 slice. Meaning, rule count and citability are unaffected. If anyone wants the markdown to mirror the PDF's list layout, the purely cosmetic fix is to split specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 14648 after 'of the function prototype; otherwise,' and move '    c) the details are taken from the external repository ... will be activated.' onto its own 4-space-indented line, matching GR 10 c) at line 14640 (and, to follow the slice convention, into the page-339 block after line 14654). This is a formatting tidy-up, not a correctness defect, and carries no spec-conformance consequence.
